system_description.narrative_title: Russia-Ukraine war intersects global fuel politics (Trump‑Putin diesel deal)
system_description.narrative_summary: A sudden political push to inject Russian diesel into global markets — led by the Trump administration's deals with Moscow — dominates the window, colliding with an intensifying Russian campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure. The energy move amplifies allied tensions and sanctions dilemmas, is portrayed by Kyiv as indirectly financing the war, and interacts with high fuel prices, midterm politics and strained intelligence/diplomatic ties. Concurrent Russian strikes (including on bridges, refineries and data centres) and Ukrainian defensive measures illustrate how military escalation and energy-market interventions form a tightly coupled system.
system_description.scope: Inside: actors (Russia, Ukraine, U.S. administration, EU, NATO), processes (diesel/energy trade, sanctions design and evasion, diplomatic negotiation, intelligence-sharing, military strikes, cyber/infra attacks), assets/events (diesel supplies/refineries, fuel logistics, data centres, bridges/transport nodes), and near-term political drivers (U.S. midterms, EU funding/conditionality).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-security and energy-market system (international order linking military conflict, energy flows, and alliance politics).
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy commodities, refining and logistics
U.S. domestic politics and electoral economy

variables.name: Global diesel supply flow
variables.description: Net volume of diesel entering global commercial markets per unit time (imports, exports, and releases combined).

variables.name: Global diesel price level
variables.description: Weighted average market price of diesel across major trading hubs measured in real terms.

variables.name: Refinery operational capacity
variables.description: Available refinery throughput as a fraction of pre-conflict baseline capacity.

variables.name: Fuel logistics resilience
variables.description: Ability of transport, storage and distribution networks to deliver fuel under disruption, measured as expected delivery performance.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement strength
variables.description: Degree to which sanctioning regimes are actively implemented and enforced, measured by compliance intensity and coverage.

variables.name: Sanctions evasion rate
variables.description: Rate at which restricted economic flows find alternative channels to bypass sanctions per unit time.

variables.name: Military strike rate
variables.description: Frequency and intensity of kinetic strikes against strategic and civilian infrastructure per unit time.

variables.name: Critical infrastructure damage level
variables.description: Aggregate functional loss across key infrastructure types (transport nodes, power, refineries, data centres) relative to baseline.

variables.name: Intelligence-sharing level
variables.description: Extent and reliability of operational intelligence exchange between aligned actors measured by volume and timeliness.

variables.name: Diplomatic trust index
variables.description: Mutual confidence between external actors in diplomatic and negotiation contexts measured by perceived reliability and cooperation willingness.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure for energy action
variables.description: Intensity of domestic political incentives and pressures pushing for immediate changes in energy supply or policy.

variables.name: Fuel price expectations
variables.description: Market and public expectations about future fuel prices and availability, measured by forward curves and sentiment indexes.

variables.name: Energy market liquidity
variables.description: Depth and ease of trading in fuel markets measured by bid-ask spreads, volumes, and ability to transact large orders without price spikes.

variables.name: Freight and shipping costs
variables.description: Average cost of moving bulk fuel and related goods across major transport routes, indexed to a baseline.

variables.name: Cyberattack frequency on infrastructure
variables.description: Rate of cyber intrusions and disruptive operations targeting critical infrastructure per unit time.

variables.name: Strategic fuel reserves level
variables.description: Quantity of government or market-held fuel stocks available for emergency release measured as days of consumption.

catalysts.title: Implementation of Trump‑Putin diesel supply deal
catalysts.description: Actual shipments or formal releases of Russian diesel into U.S. and global markets under the deal, including logistics and customs clearances. Will determine near‑term physical increases in market diesel availability.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump strikes deal with Putin to supply Russian diesel', 'Trump agrees deal with Putin for Russia to release diesel on to global market'.

catalysts.title: Congressional / legal pushback against diesel deal
catalysts.description: Legislative votes, sanctions enforcement actions, or legal rulings aimed at blocking or restricting imports stemming from the diesel agreement.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Trump's diesel agreement with Putin accused of contradicting Russia sanctions law' and broad political backlash.

catalysts.title: Ukrainian strikes on Russian fuel/refinery targets
catalysts.description: Continued Ukrainian strikes against refineries, storage or fuel logistics inside Russia that could materially reduce available diesel exports.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine says it hit Russia's largest oil refinery', 'Ukraine hits second major tech site'.

catalysts.title: Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy and transport infrastructure
catalysts.description: Ongoing Russian air and missile campaign targeting bridges, power and fuel sites in Ukraine, degrading domestic delivery and resilience.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Russian attack on Ukrainian city kills 12, a day after Trump eases diesel sanctions', 'Russia targets Ukraine’s bridges', 'Deadly Russian strikes cut power'.

catalysts.title: Allied sanctions fragmentation and evasion pressure
catalysts.description: Divergent allied positions (U.S. easing vs. Germany sticking to sanctions) increase mismatches in enforcement and create more evasion channels.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Germany sticks to Russia sanctions after Trump announcement on diesel', 'Trump strikes deal with Putin to supply Russian diesel'.

catalysts.title: High freight rates constrain US crude/diesel flows
catalysts.description: Elevated freight/shipping costs reduce attractiveness of long‑haul crude and fuel shipments from the U.S., affecting export flows and market liquidity.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Soaring freight rates threaten Asia's appetite for US crude'.

catalysts.title: Private US intermediaries engage Ukrainian / Russian talks
catalysts.description: Kushner/Witkoff and other private envoys meet Ukrainian and possibly Russian actors, shaping diplomatic options and perceptions of the diesel deal.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Witkoff, Kushner to meet Ukrainians for talks on the war', 'Trump calls for replacing Ukraine's Zelenskiy in tussle over diesel deal'.

catalysts.title: Market repricing and forward curve adjustment for diesel
catalysts.description: Traders and consumers reprice fuel expectations after IEA refusal to release additional fuel and political shifts around diesel supplies, affecting forward curves and liquidity.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Diesel price jumps after IEA says no additional fuel will be released', 'US diesel prices remain high despite Trump's moves'.
